key_insight: CoFINN adds finite-volume conservation physics to CNN-based flow prediction, making neural surrogates more physically consistent for compressible aerodynamics.
engineering_relevance: It offers a CFD-inspired deep-learning surrogate that can improve force prediction accuracy for transonic airfoil flows, especially when training data are limited.
method: Treats CNN outputs as structured finite-volume grids
Enforces conservation via numerical flux calculations in the loss
Keeps the surrogate architecture-agnostic and CFD-consistent
evidence_signal: On transonic airfoil cases at M=0.7 and Re=6×10^6, the method reduced drag prediction error by up to 34% at extreme angles of attack and by about 15% on average.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate flux formulation and grid interpretation, so implementation details may strongly affect stability and generalization.
paper_title: CoFINN: Conservation Flux Informed Neural Networks for Physics Problems Governed by Conservation Laws
